core_obligations: Define the left vertical arrow: because U refines f^{-1}V, choose a map c : I -> J with U_i contained in f^{-1}(V_{c(i)}) for all i, and set gamma(s)_{i_0...i_p} = phi(s)_{c(i_0)...c(i_p)} in degree p; this makes sense because phi induces G(V_{c(i_0)...c(i_p)}) -> F(U_{i_0...i_p}), and it is a morphism of complexes (proof lines 2556-2564).

Introduce the double complexes: with injective resolutions F -> I^bullet on X and G -> J^bullet on Y set A^{p,q} = Cech^p(U, I^q) and B^{p,q} = Cech^p(V, J^q); then choose an injective resolution f_*I -> (J')^bullet on Y together with a morphism beta : J -> (J')^bullet making equation-choice commute, and set (B')^{p,q} = Cech^p(V, (J')^q) and (B'')^{p,q} = Cech^p(V, f_*I^q) (proof lines 2565-2591).

Build the morphism of double complexes: the f-map of complexes f_*I^bullet -> I^bullet makes the same rule define gamma : (B'')^{bullet,bullet} -> A^{bullet,bullet}, which together with beta and the natural arrow (B')^{bullet,bullet} <- (B'')^{bullet,bullet} produces the displayed diagram of complexes relating Cech^bullet(U,F) to Gamma(X, I^bullet) through Tot(A^{bullet,bullet}), Tot(B^{bullet,bullet}), Tot((B')^{bullet,bullet}) and Tot((B'')^{bullet,bullet}) (proof lines 2592-2616).

Check the pieces of the diagram and conclude: the left upper pentagon commutes because equation-choice does, the two lower squares commute trivially, the right upper square commutes immediately from the definitions, hence going around the outside from Cech^bullet(V,G) to Gamma(X, I^bullet) on either side is the same after inverting the quasi-isomorphisms, which is exactly the required commutative diagram in D^+(O_X(X)) and, on cohomology, the second displayed diagram (proof lines 2617-2629).
proof_roadmap: Choose the refinement map c : I -> J and define gamma on Cech cochains by gamma(s)_{i_0...i_p} = phi(s)_{c(i_0)...c(i_p)} (proof lines 2556-2564).
Introduce A^{bullet,bullet}, B^{bullet,bullet}, the auxiliary resolution f_*I -> (J')^bullet with beta, and the double complexes (B')^{bullet,bullet}, (B'')^{bullet,bullet} (proof lines 2565-2591).
Define gamma on (B'')^{bullet,bullet} and exhibit the diagram of complexes carrying the quasi-isomorphisms (proof lines 2592-2616).
Verify commutativity of each shape and conclude that the two outer routes agree in the derived category (proof lines 2617-2629).
difficulty_reason: The lemma attaches to a morphism of ringed spaces f : X -> Y, an f-map phi : f^*G -> F and coverings U of X refining f^{-1}V a commutative diagram in D^+(O_X(X)) between the Cech complexes and derived global sections, together with its consequence for cohomology groups (statement lines 2521-2552). The proof has to build the arrow rather than invoke it: a choice function c : I -> J with U_i contained in f^{-1}(V_{c(i)}) defines gamma in every degree (proof lines 2556-2564), and then four double complexes A^{bullet,bullet}, B^{bullet,bullet}, (B')^{bullet,bullet}, (B'')^{bullet,bullet} have to be introduced, the last one using the f-map f_*I^bullet -> I^bullet, together with a third injective resolution f_*I -> (J')^bullet and a morphism beta making equation-choice commute (proof lines 2565-2591). The remaining work is the bookkeeping of the displayed diagram: which shapes commute, and why the two outer routes from Cech^bullet(V,G) to Gamma(X, I^bullet) agree after inverting quasi-isomorphisms (proof lines 2617-2629). The specific difficulty is that these double complexes are not defined in the counted statement but only inside the proof of the Cech-to-cohomology comparison, so two injective resolutions plus a third one for f_*I^bullet have to be kept coherent at once while every square of the diagram is checked. The claim is H2.
